title: A Grove Instance can be an execution venue rather than a position: the Curve pool instances have no deposit or withdrawal limits at all
content:
The Curve RLUSD/USDC Pool instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.6.1) records `N/A - swap only` for its inflow RateLimitID, outflow RateLimitID, deposit limits and withdrawal limits (A...6.1.2.3.1, A...6.1.2.3.2, A...6.1.2.4.1, A...6.1.2.4.2). Only the swap key and swap limits are populated.

So an Instance is not necessarily a place Grove keeps capital. Here it is a **capability grant scoped to one pool**: permission to exchange RLUSD and USDC at a specific address under a specific size and slippage bound, with no authority to provide liquidity to it. The Liquidity Layer's `addLiquidityCurve` and `removeLiquidityCurve` functions exist (A...2.1.2.8.2, A...2.1.2.8.3) but cannot be used against this pool, because their rate-limit keys are unset and `triggerRateLimitDecrease` reverts on a zero `maxAmount` (A...1.3.4).

The unset limits are therefore not an omission — they are the mechanism enforcing the scope. This is the fail-closed default doing useful work: the same property that makes an unconfigured instance inert makes a *partially* configured one precisely bounded.

A...6.1.3 confirms the distinction is intentional by listing a separate instance for the same pool: "Curve RLUSD/USDC Pool **LP Deposits** Instance Configuration Document" (A...6.3). Swapping through a pool and providing liquidity to it are modelled as two instances of one venue, because they are two different risks — one is execution, the other is impermanent-loss and pool-composition exposure.

The instance template strains slightly under two-sided venues: A...6.1.2.2.2 and A...6.1.2.2.3 are both titled "Underlying Asset Address", one holding USDC and the other RLUSD, because the schema assumes a single underlying.
description: Inflow and outflow RateLimitIDs and limits are all recorded as N/A - swap only, so the Instance concept covers venues Grove passes through as well as places it holds capital.
